$comment: Single source of truth for every image on the site. Read by src/data/images.ts (which turns keys into optimized imports), by scripts/generate-placeholders.mjs (which draws a labelled plate for anything still missing), and by scripts/images-readme.mjs (which regenerates src/assets/images/README.md). Add an image here first, then everywhere else follows. 'status' is either 'real' (a genuine asset is in place) or 'placeholder' (awaiting a real file from the client).

images.purpose: The PrimeTrack Telematics logo. Transparent background, square. Sourced from the live site.

A commercial vehicle or small fleet on a Rwandan road. Kigali arterial, a provincial highway, or a depot yard. Wide framing with room on the left for the headline. Shot in daylight, no heavy filters. Should read as a working vehicle, not a showroom shot.

images.usedOn: Homepage, AI video telematics feature section
images.purpose: Driver's-eye or in-cab view showing a road-facing camera in position, or a control-room screen with a live vehicle feed. Must not be a fabricated software interface.
A truck refuelling, a fuel tank sensor being fitted, or a depot fuel bay. Real hands-on work rather than a stock photo of a fuel gauge.
A phone held in hand showing the PrimeTrack mobile app. Portrait orientation. Use a real screenshot of the real app, never a mocked-up interface.

images.usedOn: Video Trackers product page and product cards
images.purpose: Dashcam and DVR unit. Carried over from the live site. Low resolution and generic; replacing it with a photo of the actual Ai-PRIME hardware would be a clear improvement.

images.usedOn: Solar Trackers product page and product cards
images.purpose: The actual PrimeSOLAR device. The image currently on the live site is a generic solar power bank, not a tracker, so it is deliberately not carried over. A photo of the real unit, ideally mounted on a truck, is needed.

images.usedOn: Fuel Trackers product page and product cards
images.purpose: A capacitive fuel level sensor or in-line flow meter, either as a product shot or installed in a tank. Close, technical framing.

images.usedOn: STAR Trackers product page and product cards
images.purpose: A STAR tracker unit, ideally magnetised onto a shipping container so the scale and the mounting are both obvious.

images.usedOn: Fleet Trackers product page and product cards
images.purpose: The GPS tracking unit itself, or an installer fitting one behind a dashboard. Should communicate hardware rather than software.

images.usedOn: eCT Systems product page and product cards
images.purpose: PrimeTrack-branded electronic cargo smart padlock with its unlocking methods called out. Genuine branded product imagery carried over from the live site. A higher-resolution version would still be welcome.
A fleet manager working across the PrimeTrack platform, or a control room in use. Real screens only, never an invented dashboard.
A professional driver at the wheel of a commercial vehicle, shot respectfully. A driver briefing or coaching session also works.
Technical or operational team working with fleet data on desktop systems. Avoid the abstract code-on-a-screen cliche.
The PrimeTrack Rwanda office at Yyussa City Centre, Kigali, or the team at work there. Helps a visitor confirm the company is physically present.
A PrimeTrack technician fitting or servicing a device on a customer vehicle. This is the single strongest credibility image on the site: it shows real people doing the actual work.

images.usedOn: Open Graph and Twitter card fallback, every page
images.purpose: Social share card. Logo plus a short line of text on a dark background works well. Must stay legible when scaled down to a thumbnail.
